Technology stocks were edging slightly higher Friday afternoon, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding less than 0.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.4% gain.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Flextronics International ( FLEX ) fell to a 20-month low on Friday, sliding to its lowest share price since September 2016 at $13.30 a share, after reporting fiscal Q4 net income lagging Wall Street estimates and providing below-consensus Q1 earnings guidance and prompting a downgrade to Market Perform from Strong Buy by analysts at Raymond James. It earned $0.28 per share during the quarter ended March 31, down from $0.29 per shre during the same quarter last year and trailing the Capital IQ consensus by $0.02 per share. Revenue grew 9% year over year to $6.41 billion from $5.86 billion during the year-ago period and topping the $6.27 billion analyst mean. The contract electronics manufacturer is projecting net income for the current quarter ending June 30 in a range of $0.22 to $0.26 per share on between $6.3 billion to $6.7 billion in revenue. The Street is at $0.32 per share on $6.3 billion in revenue.
In other sector news:
+ Microsoft ( MSFT ) rose Friday after the software and hardware giant reported fiscal Q3 net income of $0.95 per share, rising 36% over year-ago levels and beat the Capital IQ consensus call by $0.10 per share. Revenue climbed 16% over the year-ago period to $26.8 billion, also surpassing the $25.7 billion Street call.
- Intel ( INTC ) was fractionally lower in Friday trade dispite reporting adjusted Q1 net income of $0.87 per share and blowing past the Capital IQ consensus expecting $0.72 per share. Revenue rose 13% over year-ago levels to $16.1 billion, also topping the $15.07 billion Street view. It also issued above-consensus Q2 guidance, prompting an upgrade for Intel shares at Bernstein to Market Perform from Underperform while RBC Capital IQ raised its price target by $4 to $58 a share.
